metadata.title: Meta Stock Rises as U.S. Backs Lighter AI Rules Amid $145 Billion Push

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), the social-media and AI infrastructure giant, advanced approximately 1.0% to $578.31 Tuesday as Washington pushed back against sweeping new AI regulation. CEO Mark Zuckerberg was scheduled to address G20 ministers by video, putting Meta directly inside a debate that could shape the economics of its enormous AI buildout.
The proposed Carolina Principles support foundational research, commercial AI development and new regulation only when the technology creates genuinely new risks. The U.S. also rejects adding more international regulatory bodies. That lighter approach could remove a major headache for Meta as its 2026 capital-spending forecast surges to between $130 billion and $145 billion.
The valuation signal is hard to ignore: Meta's $578.31 share price stands 31.64% below its $845.92 GF Value estimate. But cheaper regulation does not guarantee stronger returns. Meta spent $31.08 billion on capital projects last quarter and generated only $784 million in free cash flowa nearly 40-to-one gap. Investors now need proof that this AI spending machine can become a cash-generating machine.
